problem: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for visual navigation is a fast-growing research area, but the literature lacks a systematic organization of end-to-end DRL methods that map raw high-dimensional images directly to navigation policies.
motivation: Visual navigation is a basic capability that artificial agents need in order to interact with their environment and to support more advanced behaviors. DRL lets an agent learn a navigation policy end-to-end from images, which has made it a research hotspot in AI and robotics. A structured review can clarify the main method families and the problems that remain open.
key_idea: The survey organizes DRL-based visual navigation into five categories — direct, hierarchical, multi-task, memory-inference and vision-language DRL navigation — after first giving background on RL, DL and DRL, and closes with challenges and opportunities.
insight: This is a survey, so it has no experiments or ablations. Its main contribution is the five-way taxonomy, which separates methods by what they add to plain end-to-end DRL: hierarchy (policy decomposition), multi-task learning, memory/inference for partial observability, and language grounding. Only the abstract is available, so the paper's specific analytic conclusions cannot be verified.
method: Background overview: introduces reinforcement learning, deep learning and deep reinforcement learning as foundations.
Direct DRL vNavigation: end-to-end policies mapping raw images to actions.
Hierarchical DRL vNavigation: methods that decompose navigation into high- and low-level policies.
Multi-task DRL vNavigation: methods that learn several navigation tasks or auxiliary tasks jointly.
Memory-inference DRL vNavigation: methods using memory and inference to handle partial observability.
Vision-language DRL vNavigation: methods that ground natural-language instructions in visual navigation.
Challenges and opportunities: discussion of open problems and future directions for visual DRL navigation.

results: No experimental results; this is a survey. It reviews visual DRL navigation in detail under five categories (direct, hierarchical, multi-task, memory-inference, vision-language) and discusses challenges and possible opportunities.
limitations: Survey from 2020: it predates the large-model (LLM/VLM) and foundation-model era of embodied navigation, as well as many modular and map-based approaches.
Focused on DRL end-to-end methods, so it likely gives less attention to modular, classical SLAM-based or imitation-learning pipelines.
Only the abstract was available, so the depth of coverage and any benchmark comparisons cannot be assessed.
